**Continuous 2.30.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.30.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.30.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.30.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.30.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.30.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.30.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.30.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.30.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.30.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.30.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.30.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.28.0

This release is about long conversations on a local server such as Strata or llama.cpp. When a conversation outgrew the context window, the oldest messages were dropped a few at a time on most turns, and every drop made the server read the whole conversation again (about 85 s for 394k tokens). Now nothing is dropped until 85% of the window, and then a whole block goes at once, so the turns after it reuse the cache. Before that point, planned compaction fixes where a summary would cut, writes the summary in the background while you are idle, and lets **Compact now** apply it at once; the context meter shows what compacting would cost in seconds or dollars, and a message that would force a full re-read waits and offers to compact first. The compaction summary now goes after the system prompt instead of inside it, so compacting no longer invalidates the cached system prompt and tools.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- Strata, llama.cpp and vLLM: the token estimate is calibrated from the server's own `prompt_tokens` after each answered request, per model (between 0.6 and 2, with 5% headroom; a single request outside 0.7 to 1.5 times the current ratio is ignored). Ollama, LM Studio and other local servers, which may leave cached tokens out of the count, keep only the existing overflow correction. Qwen models, which the Llama 2 tokenizer over-counts by about 23%, get about 97k tokens of a 524k window back. Hosted providers are unchanged.
- **A line when a compaction is prepared.** When planned compaction has made its summary in the background, a quiet line above the input says so, with the turns it covers. On a local server it waits for you: "Compaction prepared (summary of turns 1–80 ready); Compact now applies it in about 12 s (not pre-warmed)." **Compact now** applies it and keeps the newest turns word for word; **Not now** hides it (Compact now can still use the summary). Nothing is re-read until you choose it. On a cloud provider with planned compaction turned on, the summary applies at your next message, which writes the cache anyway.
- **A hold before a forced re-read.** When your message would take the conversation past the point where the oldest turns are dropped to fit (85% of the window on a local server, 90% on cloud), the message waits and the line offers **Compact now, then send** (with the estimate; instant when a summary is ready) or **Continue anyway**. Enter chooses Compact now; Continue anyway needs a click or Tab then Enter, and a held-down key chooses nothing.
- **The cost of Compact now.** The context meter's details show an estimate next to **Compact now**: in dollars on a cloud model, and in seconds on a Strata server (from its `/metrics`).
- **Pre-warm on Strata and llama.cpp (experimental, off by default).** With `contextManagement.prewarm: local`, once the summary is ready and you are still idle, the conversation as it will be after compacting is sent to the server once with a one-token reply, so your next message applies the summary with nothing to read again ("prepared and pre-warmed"). On Strata it pins the server's checkpoint at the end of the summary, and it is skipped, with the reason, when Strata reports less free memory than it could take. It has not been checked on a live Strata server yet: turn it on after the steps in the local servers page ("Planned compaction and the pre-warm"). The prepared line says once that it is off.
- **Planned compaction on local servers.** Once a conversation passes 70% of the model's context window, the point where a compaction would cut is fixed and stays put as the conversation grows. After 10 seconds with nothing streaming and no typing, the summary of everything before that point is made in the background as a separate request; nothing in the chat changes. **Compact now** then applies it at once, with no wait and no second summary request, and the newest turns stay word for word. A short first request is quoted word for word above the summary. Typing, sending a message or a running tool stops the background summary, and it is tried again at the next pause. Editing an earlier message throws the prepared summary away.
- **`contextManagement.plannedCompaction`** in a model's config turns this on or off. It is on by default for a server on this machine or network, and off for cloud providers, where the background request costs money. Set it to `false` to turn it off, or `true` to use it with a cloud provider.

### Behaviour changes

- A long conversation is trimmed in whole blocks: nothing is dropped until the prompt passes 85% of the window (local servers) or 90% (hosted providers); then the oldest messages go at once, down to 60% or 65%, and the prompt grows append-only, reusing the prompt cache, until it passes the threshold again. A compaction summary is never dropped; blocks are counted from the turns after it. The context meter's prune line shows the new threshold.
- The configured `maxTokens` is reserved for the reply, up to 10% of the window and at least 1,000 tokens, instead of a fixed 1,000 tokens.
- A planned compaction's verbatim tail is capped at 65,536 tokens (it was 64,000), the same table as the block drop.
- The cache-miss reasons name compaction correctly: a summary no longer changes the system prompt, so "the system prompt changed" now says "the base prompt or a rule", and a shorter prompt is "a compaction, or the oldest messages left out to fit".
- Compacted turns are still kept in the saved session and shown above the summary, as before. With a prepared summary, **Compact now** summarises up to the planned point and keeps the newest turns (up to 15% of the window, at most 64,000 tokens) instead of summarising the whole conversation.
- After **Compact**, the conversation summary is sent as the first message after the system message instead of being added to the system message. The tools and the system message are now the same bytes before and after a compaction, so the provider keeps them cached (an Anthropic or Bedrock breakpoint on the system prompt, a local server's system-prompt checkpoint) and only the summary and the turns after it are read again. A rule that only a summarised turn matched is sent with the summary.

### Fixes

- In the `cn` command line, `Fetch` now asks before reading a URL that carries a long encoded value or credentials, and before reading a name that does not resolve and has no public top-level domain (`http://wiki.corp/`, `http://nas.lan/`), as the IDE does. Headless runs refuse these calls. Both checks were skipped at the default levels.
- A single-label name that does not resolve here, such as `http://wiki/` or `http://jenkins/`, now asks before a model fetch in the IDE and in `cn`, even when the label is also a public top-level domain (`.wiki`, `.app`). Behind a proxy such a name is usually an internal host.
- Once a conversation was over the window, the cut moved by a message or two on most turns because its size depended on the latest turn, and every move made a local server read the whole conversation again (about 85 s for 394k tokens on Strata). The cut now moves only forward, once per block.
- On Claude models that check that earlier reasoning still matches the conversation (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable and Mythos 5.1 and 5.2), compacting at an earlier response no longer sends back the reasoning of the turns it kept. That reasoning was produced with the summarised turns in front of it, and sending it after the summary could be refused with an error. Reasoning produced after the compaction is still sent.

### Upgrade notes

- **One full prompt read after upgrading.** A session compacted by an earlier release reads its prompt once, because its summary moves out of the system prompt.
- **Pre-warm is off by default.** It is experimental: turn it on with `contextManagement.prewarm: local` on a Strata or llama.cpp server. The local servers page lists the checks to confirm it works on your server.
- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host. On a Strata server the extension reads `/metrics` and `/v1/status` on the same server you configured.
